title: Bijectivity of the middle localization comparison
statement: Under the Mayer–Vietoris localization diagram and local comparison hypotheses, the middle comparison additive homomorphism is bijective in every degree.

proof.text: Apply exists_cohomologySection_division to the given nonvanishing open S to obtain injectivity of multiplication by every tensor power of s on every restricted cohomology group. Cancel multiplication in the formulas for c and any other comparison. Equality on every fraction implies equality of additive homomorphisms: precompose with the quotient map, use DirectSum.addHom_ext, and use surjectivity of the quotient map. Apply localizedCohomology_mayerVietoris, identify its open with S by SetLike.coe_injective, and identify its comparison family with c by this uniqueness.

Identify the three local equivalences with c U p, c V p and c (U intersect V) p by the same uniqueness. Their bijectivity gives bijectivity of the intersection and product comparisons; the latter is proved componentwise using the local injections and surjections. Bundle the lower restriction pair, difference, and connecting maps as additive homomorphisms. Transport lower exactness and the initial injection along the intersection and union equalities. Restriction along an identity is an identity by NatTrans.rightDerived_id; hence this transport does not change the maps. The three supplied pointwise squares give equalities of composites by AddMonoidHom.ext.

In degree zero apply Mathlib AddMonoidHom.bijective_of_bijective_of_injective_of_left_exact to the union-product-intersection rows. The two rows are exact at the product, both initial maps are injective, the product comparison is bijective, and the intersection comparison is injective. These are precisely the hypotheses of this degree-zero five-lemma variant.

For p = q + 1 apply Mathlib AddMonoidHom.bijective_of_surjective_of_bijective_of_bijective_of_injective to the five terms product in degree q, intersection in degree q, union in degree q+1, product in degree q+1, intersection in degree q+1. Use the upper and reindexed lower exactness at the three interior terms, the four commuting squares, and the local comparison bijections. The middle comparison is c (U union V) (q+1). The zero and successor cases prove the conclusion for all p.

theorem localized_middle_comparison_bijective
    (X : Scheme.{u_1}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (s : Γ(L, ⊤))
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (S : X.Opens) (hS : (S : Set X) = nonvanishingLocus L s)
    (U V : X.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X)) (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
    (c : ∀ (W : X.Opens) (p : ℕ), CohomologyFractionPresentation L F s p W →+
      (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p (W ⊓ S)).obj F)
    (hc : ∀ (W : X.Opens) (p n : ℕ)
        (ξ : (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p W).obj
          (F ⊗ L.tensorPow n : X.Modules)),
      (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p (W ⊓ S)).map
          (((ρ_ F).inv ≫ F ◁ tensorPowSection (homOfGlobalSection L s) n) :
            F ⟶ (F ⊗ L.tensorPow n : X.Modules))
          (c W p (cohomologyFraction L F s p W n ξ)) =
        (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomologyRestriction X.toRingedSpace p
          (homOfLE (inf_le_left : W ⊓ S ≤ W))).app
            (F ⊗ L.tensorPow n : X.Modules) ξ)
    (h_locU : ∀ p : ℕ, ∃ e : CohomologyFractionPresentation L F s p U ≃+
        (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p (U ⊓ S)).obj F,
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (ξ : (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p U).obj
          (F ⊗ L.tensorPow n : X.Modules)),
        (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p (U ⊓ S)).map
            (((ρ_ F).inv ≫ F ◁ tensorPowSection (homOfGlobalSection L s) n) :
              F ⟶ (F ⊗ L.tensorPow n : X.Modules))
            (e (cohomologyFraction L F s p U n ξ)) =
          (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomologyRestriction X.toRingedSpace p
            (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U ⊓ S ≤ U))).app
              (F ⊗ L.tensorPow n : X.Modules) ξ)
    (h_locV : ∀ p : ℕ, ∃ e : CohomologyFractionPresentation L F s p V ≃+
        (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p (V ⊓ S)).obj F,
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (ξ : (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p V).obj
          (F ⊗ L.tensorPow n : X.Modules)),
        (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p (V ⊓ S)).map
            (((ρ_ F).inv ≫ F ◁ tensorPowSection (homOfGlobalSection L s) n) :
              F ⟶ (F ⊗ L.tensorPow n : X.Modules))
            (e (cohomologyFraction L F s p V n ξ)) =
          (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomologyRestriction X.toRingedSpace p
            (homOfLE (inf_le_left : V ⊓ S ≤ V))).app
              (F ⊗ L.tensorPow n : X.Modules) ξ)
    (h_locUV : ∀ p : ℕ, ∃ e : CohomologyFractionPresentation L F s p (U ⊓ V) ≃+
        (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p (U ⊓ V ⊓ S)).obj F,
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (ξ : (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p (U ⊓ V)).obj
          (F ⊗ L.tensorPow n : X.Modules)),
        (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p (U ⊓ V ⊓ S)).map
            (((ρ_ F).inv ≫ F ◁ tensorPowSection (homOfGlobalSection L s) n) :
              F ⟶ (F ⊗ L.tensorPow n : X.Modules))
            (e (cohomologyFraction L F s p (U ⊓ V) n ξ)) =
          (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomologyRestriction X.toRingedSpace p
            (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U ⊓ V ⊓ S ≤ U ⊓ V))).app
              (F ⊗ L.tensorPow n : X.Modules) ξ) :
    ∀ p : ℕ, Function.Bijective (c (U ⊔ V) p)
